name: @juscribe/mcp

tools.name: get_workspace_summary
tools.description: Get a condensed overview of the workspace board: panel counts, projects, velocity, users, and ticket summaries for the current and backlog panels unless others are named. Release, milestone and deadline markers are included, and counted. Use this to orient yourself before drilling into specific tickets.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

panels.description: Comma-separated panel names to include ticket details for (default "current,backlog"): icebox, backlog, current, done, which the board shows as Icebox, Backlog, Current and Done. Panels not listed return only count/points.

tools.name: list_tickets
tools.description: List tickets in a workspace with optional filters — panel, state, type, project, assignee, label, iteration, what changed since a moment, when they were created, when they are due, or a search — 50 to a page, in board order or by due date. A panel comes with its release, milestone and deadline markers. The reply says when more pages exist, and when markers were left out.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

panel.description: Filter by panel, which the board shows as Icebox, Backlog, Current and Done

ticket_type.description: Filter by type (feature, bug, chore, research, milestone, release, deadline)

project_id.description: Project external ID, to list a project's tickets. Add panel to see only what is left.

requester_id.description: Only tickets this person asked for, by user ID. For "what did I ask for?"

stakeholder_id.description: Only tickets this person decides on as stakeholder, by user ID

updated_since.description: Only tickets changed after this moment, as a date or an ISO 8601 time (2026-09-22, or 2026-09-22T09:00:00Z). For "what changed since Monday?"

label.description: Only tickets carrying this label, by name as list_labels shows it

iteration_id.description: Only tickets in this iteration, by its number from list_iterations, or none for tickets in no iteration

created_after.description: Only tickets created on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD

created_before.description: Only tickets created on or before this date, YYYY-MM-DD

due_after.description: Only tickets due on or after this date, YYYY-MM-DD. For "what is due this week?"

due_before.description: Only tickets due on or before this date, YYYY-MM-DD

sort.description: due_date: soonest due first, undated last. recent: most recently finished first. Unset: board order.

include_markers.description: Include release, milestone and deadline markers. On by default when panel is given, off otherwise

tools.name: get_ticket
tools.description: Get full details for a single ticket, including comments and attachments.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

comments_limit.description: Only the newest N comments, oldest first (default: all)

tools.name: create_ticket
tools.description: Create a new ticket in the workspace. Returns the created ticket, with notes when it matches another ticket. A new ticket goes to the bottom of the Backlog. When the person asks for the Icebox, it goes to the top of the Icebox. Place one anywhere else only when the person asks. In the description, Open with a sentence or two in plain words saying what happened or what is asked, before any detail. Write #123 only for a ticket number, and p45 for a project.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

points.description: Effort estimate in points (0, 1, 2, 3, 5, or 8): how much work the ticket takes. Not a time estimate, and not a rating of how complex or difficult the work is. Every ticket has points before it starts: estimate them yourself, or use the person's number when they give one.

project_id.description: Project external ID to assign to

assignee_ids.description: User IDs to assign, from list_people

labels.description: Label names, as list_labels shows them

panel.description: Which panel the ticket goes in: backlog (the default) or icebox. A new ticket goes to the bottom of the Backlog. When the person asks for the Icebox, it goes to the top of the Icebox. Place one anywhere else only when the person asks.

insert_at.description: Where in the panel: top, bottom, before:<ticket id> or after:<ticket id>

due_date.description: Due date as YYYY-MM-DD, on any ticket; it has to be in the future. Set one only when the person gives a date.

tools.name: get_attachment
tools.description: Read a file attached to a ticket, from get_ticket's attachments: a photo comes back as an image, a PDF or a text, CSV, Markdown or JSON file as text. A long file is cut at 150,000 characters and says so; an archive or other kind is refused by name, with the ticket's link so the person can open it in the app.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

tools.name: attach_file
tools.description: Save something you wrote — a newsletter draft, a volunteer list, meeting notes — onto a ticket as a Markdown (.md), text (.txt) or CSV (.csv) file. Only those kinds: a photo or PDF shown to you in chat cannot be passed on as bytes, and for those the answer is the ticket's link so the person can add the file in the app.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

filename.description: The file name with its extension: .md, .txt or .csv

tools.name: attach_upload
tools.description: Attach a photo or PDF the person added to this chat onto a ticket. Pass the file itself as file. This works only where the chat app hands the file to the tool, as ChatGPT does; anywhere else, or for another kind of file, the answer is the ticket's link so the person can add it in the app. For something you wrote, use attach_file.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

file.description: The file the person added to this chat

annotations.title: Attach a file the person added

tools.name: create_tickets
tools.description: File a list of tasks in one call, such as the action items from meeting notes. Every item is checked as create_ticket checks one, and one bad item stops the whole batch before anything is written. Items go to the bottom of the Backlog in the order given; an item whose panel is icebox goes to the top of the Icebox, which the person has to ask for. Place one elsewhere afterwards with move_ticket. The reply says what happened to each item.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

points.description: Effort estimate in points (0, 1, 2, 3, 5, or 8): how much work the ticket takes. Not a time estimate, and not a rating of how complex or difficult the work is. Every ticket has points before it starts: estimate them yourself, or use the person's number when they give one.

project_id.description: Project external ID to assign to

assignee_ids.description: User IDs to assign, from list_people

labels.description: Label names, as list_labels shows them

panel.description: Which panel the ticket goes in: the bottom of the Backlog when unset, the top of the Icebox when icebox, which the person has to ask for

due_date.description: Due date as YYYY-MM-DD, on any ticket; it has to be in the future. Set one only when the person gives a date.

tickets.description: The tickets to file, in order

tools.name: update_ticket
tools.description: Update an existing ticket's fields. Only provided fields are changed. Before changing a description, read the ticket with get_ticket first. Text a person wrote stays word for word, with anything you add below a --- line, and you edit your own earlier additions in place, so they are not stacked as dated updates. To only add below the text, use append_to_description.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

description.description: New description, replacing the whole text. Before changing a description, read the ticket with get_ticket first. Text a person wrote stays word for word, with anything you add below a --- line, and you edit your own earlier additions in place, so they are not stacked as dated updates. To only add below the text, use append_to_description.

points.description: Effort estimate in points (0, 1, 2, 3, 5, or 8): how much work the ticket takes. Not a time estimate, and not a rating of how complex or difficult the work is. Every ticket has points before it starts: estimate them yourself, or use the person's number when they give one.

project_id.description: New project external ID (null to unset)

assignee_ids.description: User IDs to assign, from list_people, replacing the current set

stakeholder_id.description: New stakeholder user ID (null to unset)

labels.description: Label names, as list_labels shows them, replacing the current set

anyOf.description: Due date as YYYY-MM-DD, on any ticket; it has to be in the future. Set one only when the person gives a date.

due_date.description: Due date as YYYY-MM-DD, on any ticket; it has to be in the future. Set one only when the person gives a date. Null to unset.

state.description: Move the ticket back to the Icebox (unprioritized) or the Backlog (prioritized); tell the person where it is going first. Moving forward is transition_ticket.

tools.name: append_to_description
tools.description: Add text to the end of a ticket's description, after a blank line. Nothing already there is changed, including an edit someone made a moment ago, and the description is not resent. Use this to add notes, findings or a plan below what a person wrote.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

tools.name: transition_ticket
tools.description: Move a ticket forward one step at a time: unprioritized → prioritized → started → finished → delivered. Give a ticket points with update_ticket before starting it. Finished is the last step you take on your own; deliver only when the person asks. Cancelled is reachable from any open state and needs a resolution. To move a ticket back to the Icebox or the Backlog, tell the person where it is going, then use update_ticket with state. Accepting or rejecting is a person's decision, made in the app, so this tool offers neither.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

tools.name: add_comment
tools.description: Add a comment to a ticket. Supports @mentions. Open with a sentence or two in plain words saying what happened or what is asked, before any detail. Write #123 only for a ticket number, and p45 for a project.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

tools.name: update_comment
tools.description: Replace the text of a comment on a ticket. Only a comment you wrote can be changed; anyone else's is refused. The comment id is in get_ticket.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

body.description: The new comment text (supports @mentions and markdown)

tools.name: delete_comment
tools.description: Delete a comment from a ticket for good. Only a comment you wrote can be deleted; anyone else's is refused. The comment id is in get_ticket.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

tools.name: move_ticket
tools.description: Put a ticket directly above (before) or below (after) another ticket in the same panel. This is how the backlog is prioritised. Moving between panels is update_ticket or transition_ticket.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

before.description: Put it directly above this ticket

after.description: Put it directly below this ticket

tools.name: get_current_iteration
tools.description: The iteration in progress: its number, dates, committed and accepted points, and its tickets, 50 to a page. Use this rather than list_iterations, which returns every iteration the board has had.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

tools.name: list_subtasks
tools.description: List a ticket's subtasks: its ordered steps, each with at most one owner. The ids here are what the other subtask tools take.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

tools.name: add_subtask
tools.description: Add a step to the end of a ticket. Place it elsewhere with move_subtask. Steps someone performs are subtasks, one action or command each, not checkboxes in the description.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

assignee_id.description: The one person who does it, from list_people

tools.name: update_subtask
tools.description: Change a subtask. Set completed to the value you want: true ticks it and false reopens it, and calling either twice changes nothing. Only the fields passed change.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

completed.description: true when the step is done, false to reopen it

assignee_id.description: The one person who does it, from list_people

tools.name: move_subtask
tools.description: Move a subtask to a place in its ticket's list, counting from 1. A place past the end moves it to the bottom.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

place.description: Where it goes: 1 is the top

tools.name: delete_subtask
tools.description: Take a step off a ticket's checklist for good. To mark one done instead, use update_subtask with completed: true.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

tools.name: list_blockers
tools.description: List what blocks a ticket, or with direction "blocks", what it blocks. Resolved blockers are included with resolved_at set. The ids here are what resolve_blocker takes.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

direction.description: blocked_by (default): what this ticket waits on. blocks: what waits on it.

tools.name: add_blocker
tools.description: Record that a ticket waits on another ticket, a project, or an outside event (External). Add one blocker per condition that clears on its own, each with a short title. A blocker with a date says only its date condition, not the other blockers.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

blocker_id.description: The ticket or project it waits on. Required for Ticket and Project.

title.description: A short label the board shows, a few words. An External blocker needs this or a description.

description.description: More detail on what is awaited

due_kind.description: What the date means: wait_until (do not start before), review_on (look again then), expected_by (should clear by then). Needs due_on.

tools.name: resolve_blocker
tools.description: Mark a blocker resolved, which unblocks the ticket once none is left. Get its id from list_blockers.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

tools.description: List all projects in a workspace with their state and position.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

tools.name: get_project
tools.description: One project in full: its description, where its plan lives, who asked for it and who owns it, and the counts of its tickets. Its tickets are list_tickets with project_id.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

tools.name: create_project
tools.description: Start a project: a name, and the description where its plan lives. It lands at the end of the list; the person orders projects in the app.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

tools.name: update_project
tools.description: Change a project's name, description, colour or stakeholder. Only the fields passed change. Moving, sealing or deleting a project is done in the app.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

stakeholder_id.description: New stakeholder user ID, from list_people (null to unset)

tools.name: list_iterations
tools.description: List iterations (sprints) for a workspace, with velocity and point data.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

tools.name: list_workspaces
tools.description: List the workspaces this connection can reach, with the ids the other tools take as workspace_id.

tools.name: create_workspace
tools.description: Create a workspace, a new board of its own. Use it only when the person asks for a new board. Juscribe allows it when the person this agent acts for is an owner of the organization and its plan has room for another; otherwise it refuses and nothing is made. Answers with the id the other tools take as workspace_id.

tools.description: List the people and agents on the board, with the user ids that assignee_ids and stakeholder_id take. Mention someone by @username: names are not unique.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

tools.description: List the labels on the board, with the ids that label_ids takes.

tools.name: create_label
tools.description: Create a label the board does not have yet, such as "fundraising" when tagging asks for one that is missing. Use it only when the person asks: a board's labels are its own vocabulary, and a near-duplicate splits every later filter. A name the board already has, in any case, is refused with the existing label.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

name.description: The label, as it will read on tickets

color.description: A colour, as #rrggbb; the palette's next when unset

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search tickets, projects, comments and people at once. Matches label and project names too, and ranks an exact ticket or project number first. Results are compact: use get_ticket for detail.

workspace_id.description: Workspace ID, as list_workspaces gives it. Defaults to the one workspace this connection reaches; required when it reaches several.

instructions:
This server reads and changes a Juscribe board: the tickets, projects and iterations of one team's workspace. Everything you do here appears on the board under your agent's name, and teammates see it as it happens.

Ticket states. A ticket moves one step at a time: unprioritized (the Icebox, not yet scheduled) → prioritized (the Backlog) → started → finished → delivered → accepted or rejected. A rejected ticket goes back to started. Start a ticket when work on it begins, and finish it when the work is done. Deliver only when the person asks: delivering hands the work over for acceptance, and a board that merges the two states delivers on finish by itself. A skipped step is refused, and the refusal names the states that are allowed next. To move a ticket back to the Icebox or the Backlog, use update_ticket with state.

Only a person accepts or rejects. Accepting or rejecting delivered work is the reviewer's decision, made in the app, so this server cannot do either.

Cancelling needs a resolution. An open ticket can be cancelled from any state, and the call must say why with one of: duplicate, wont_do, cant_reproduce, obsolete.

Where new tickets go. A ticket you create goes to the bottom of the Backlog. When the person asks for the Icebox, it goes to the top of the Icebox. Place one anywhere else only when the person asks.

References. In titles, descriptions and comments, #123 means ticket 123 and p45 means project 45, and the board turns both into links. Use them when you mention a ticket or a project, and never put # in front of a number that is not a ticket id.

Talking to people who do not code. Most people here use a chat app. Use the words the board shows, Icebox, Backlog, Current, Done, not state names, and do not narrate states. Every ticket has points before it starts: estimate them yourself, or use the person's number. When chat cannot do something, such as attaching a photo, give the item's link in the app.
